findings.title: Potential for Arbitrary File Access via JWKS URI
findings.description: While the JWK client checks for 'http' and 'https' schemes, `urllib.request` might still be influenced by internal redirections or header manipulations depending on the environment and `SSLContext` configuration.
steps_to_exploit: Supply a URL that triggers an open redirect on an attacker-controlled server.
The `PyJWKClient` follows the redirect to an unintended destination.
If the internal environment permits, the client may be forced to reach internal-only resources.

findings.title: JWKS URI Scheme Confusion
findings.description: While `PyJWKClient` filters schemes, it relies on standard `urllib` which may process unintended schemes if the validation is bypassed or if internal redirects within the library's dependencies occur.
steps_to_exploit: Supply a file-based or secondary URI to `PyJWKClient` if the URL parsing can be circumvented via variations.
Trigger the library to perform a 'fetch' on a local system resource.
Expose sensitive local files via the JWK endpoint response.
findings.impact: Local File Disclosure or SSRF via configuration.
